plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bid half of your value. This is because any bid higher than half your value risks winning the auction and paying too much, while any bid lower risks losing the auction when winning would have been profitable. My value is $24, so half is $12. I will bid $12.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges on bidding slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $49, a reasonable assumption is that others will bid around half of their value. With my value at $9, I want to win against bids likely below $9/2 = $4.50. Bidding $4.60 secures a win against bids up to $4.50, while minimizing potential overpayment.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0 and $49, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is (2/3) * 49 = 32.67. To maximize profit, bid slightly above this, but considering my own value of $13, I should bid conservatively. Bidding too high risks paying more than the item is worth to me.
